findings.summary: Accepted as proved: if a finite noncollinear subset of Z^2 is preserved by a nonidentity Euclidean rotation about an arbitrary center, the rotation is a half-turn or quarter-turn. The proof derives a rational rotation matrix from three noncollinear lattice points, obtains finite order from the induced permutation, and uses the rational algebraic-integer trace to exclude every other finite rotation order. This closes the missing arbitrary-center lemma in the earlier rotational classification; noncollinearity is essential, and reflections or affine and approximate symmetries are outside scope.

Accepted as proved: any 153-point no-three-in-line subset of G_77 has no nonidentity rotational symmetry about any center. The rotation-classification lemma leaves only half-turns and quarter-turns; odd cardinality forces inclusion of a half-turn center, creating a collinear opposite pair through that center, while 153 mod 4 forces inclusion of a quarter-turn center and the squared half-turn gives the same obstruction. This is only a symmetry restriction and does not prove that a 153-point set is nonexistent; reflection-symmetric and asymmetric possibilities remain.

Accepted as proved: if a 154-point no-three-in-line subset of G_77 has nontrivial rotational symmetry, it must be invariant under the half-turn about (38,38), with (38,38) unselected. Quarter-turn symmetry is excluded by orbit cardinalities; equality in the row and column bounds forces exactly two selected points in every row and column and hence bounding box [0,76]^2; invariance of that box forces the half-turn center to be (38,38); even cardinality excludes selection of the unique fixed point. This neither establishes existence nor identifies every centered-half-turn configuration with the narrower rct4 class.

The exact value remains undecided and no bound improvement is established: the certified interval stays 152 <= D(77) <= 154. The contribution gives neither a 153- or 154-point coordinate certificate, an impossibility proof for either size, nor a global exhaustive search. It only constrains symmetry classes: a 153-point set cannot be rotationally symmetric; a rotationally symmetric 154-point set must have the centered half-turn; asymmetric, reflection-symmetric, and general centered-half-turn cases remain possible in principle, and centered-half-turn symmetry is broader than rct4.
